what_the_class_is: The whole distortion type as far as anything measured reaches it: the pair summed to one path, the drive byte as a gain into a memoryless curve, and the level, tone and pan stages the type prints. No ladder was ever made on this type, so its pre-gain and post-gain are fitted on the two ends of its own drive sweep. The cabinet is not drawn. The candidates differ only in the curve.

era.when: Mid nineteen-nineties, a custom fixed-point DSP running its effects at a fixed clock with a small control processor beside it.
what_that_implies: A fixed-point accumulator in saturating mode is a hard clip for nothing: the curve that costs no instruction at all.
A smooth curve costs a table or a polynomial; the cubic is the cheapest polynomial that reaches its ceiling with a flat slope, a tanh needs a table.
Nothing is oversampled: a curve runs at the clock the rest of the effect runs at and what it puts above half of it folds back.
era.would_be_wrong_if: The order series of a drive sweep read at settings no gain here was fitted on falls away at high orders in a way none of the three curves produces, or the orders stop following the drive byte as a gain.

candidates.reading: The drive byte is a gain in front of a hard clip; the gains either side of it are fitted per candidate on takes no stage compares, and on the two settings of the sweep the drive claim cites.
candidates.predicts: Orders past the knee falling as a power of the order, a kink's slope, and the sharpest ceiling of the three: the output stops moving within a few decibels of the knee.

candidates.reading: The drive byte is a gain in front of a tanh; the gains either side of it are fitted per candidate on takes no stage compares, and on the two settings of the sweep the drive claim cites.
candidates.predicts: Orders falling faster than any power of the order high up, and the softest approach to the ceiling of the three.

candidates.reading: The drive byte is a gain in front of a cubic; the gains either side of it are fitted per candidate on takes no stage compares, and on the two settings of the sweep the drive claim cites.
candidates.predicts: Orders falling as a steeper power than the clip's, and a small-signal slope half again over unity that the pre-gain absorbs, so its ceiling is reached from further down the drive byte.

what_no_candidate_here_predicts: Anything the amp switch or the amp type does: the response they put after the curve has no filter here.
Even orders the curve makes itself: all three curves are odd.
Content off the whole multiples of a steady tone other than what folds back from above half the clock.
